age: Patients with a critical COVID-19 course, as well as healthy controls (≥18 years of age), were enrolled in this study between 6 November 2020 and 22 February 2021.

cell_line.evidence: To evaluate the performance of the nanoLC-MS system, a complex external standard (digest of the human cell line A549) was measured at the start, middle, and end of the study series.

cell_type.evidence: A comparative proteome analysis of highly purified platelets from critically diseased COVID-19 patients with different outcomes (survivors and non-survivors) and age- and sex-matched controls was performed.

developmental_stage: Patients with a critical COVID-19 course, as well as healthy controls (≥18 years of age), were enrolled in this study between 6 November 2020 and 22 February 2021.

disease_state.evidence: A comparative proteome analysis of highly purified platelets from critically diseased COVID-19 patients with different outcomes (survivors and non-survivors) and age- and sex-matched controls was performed.

material_type: A comparative proteome analysis of highly purified platelets from critically diseased COVID-19 patients with different outcomes (survivors and non-survivors) and age- and sex-matched controls was performed.

sample_source.evidence: Venous blood samples were collected after admission to the intensive care unit (ICU) of the HDZ NRW (median: 2 days after admission).

species.evidence: The MaxQuant software (v.2.0.3.1, , accessed on 28 August 2023) was employed for the comprehensive analysis of the DDA raw data. Spectra were meticulously searched against the human reference proteome (UP000005640) from the UniProtKB database (release 2021_11), utilizing specific parameters.

tissue.evidence: Platelets, the smallest cells in human blood, known for their role in primary hemostasis, are also able to interact with pathogens and play a crucial role in the immune response.
